Marylou's Remarkable Yellowfin Tuna Fishing Adventure in San José del Cabo

Fishing Report Nov 11 Written by EXOTIC FISH-CABO

A Remarkable Yellowfin Tuna Battle in San José del Cabo

November 2025 brought an unforgettable fishing experience for Marylou in the waters off San José del Cabo.

Joining Exotic Fish Cabo for a private fishing adventure departing from Puerto Los Cabos Marina, Marylou was ready to enjoy a day on the ocean and take on one of the region's most exciting game fish.

What followed was an extraordinary test of patience, strength, and determination.

The highlight of her trip came when she hooked into a large yellowfin tuna, a species famous for its powerful runs and remarkable endurance.

As the fish pulled hard against the line, Marylou faced the challenge herself, carefully managing the rod and reel through a demanding battle.

The tuna refused to surrender easily, repeatedly testing her strength as she worked to bring it closer to the boat.

With determination and the crew's support, Marylou continued the fight until she finally brought the impressive fish alongside the boat.

It was a memorable achievement and a perfect example of why yellowfin tuna fishing attracts anglers from around the world to Los Cabos.

Sometimes, the most rewarding fishing experiences aren't simply about the size of the catch. They're about overcoming a challenge, enjoying the ocean, and creating a memory that stays with you long after returning to shore.

For Marylou, this was certainly one of those moments.

Trip Highlights

  • Date: November 2025

  • Departure: Puerto Los Cabos Marina, San José del Cabo

  • Angler: Marylou

  • Species caught: Yellowfin tuna

  • Catch highlight: Large yellowfin tuna brought alongside the boat

  • Experience: Private fishing charter

Yellowfin tuna are known for their speed, strength, and ability to make powerful runs during a fight.

Their activity around San José del Cabo depends on water temperatures, currents, bait availability, and seasonal conditions.

Every trip is different, and catches are never guaranteed.
